summary: Seven experiments occupied 84 minutes: one compute-bound experiment and six synthesis-only experiments. The 66-minute context transition, not the compute-bound entry recorded at 0 minutes, was the dominant operational cost.
bottlenecks_identified: The synthesis-only transition of .504 terminal evidence into .505 execution context took 66 minutes, making milestone handoff the primary bottleneck.
Cached local-SOTA parser forensics, repair, and positive control took 18 minutes, making parser-control preparation the secondary bottleneck.
improvements_suggested: Generate the next milestone's execution context mechanically from terminal evidence, then validate the generated handoff before launch.
Persist parser diagnostics and the positive control as a reusable preflight bundle so parser forensics is not reconstructed during the milestone.
Record task-scoped GPU utilization between each compute-bound start and finish, together with declared model count, so an idle monitor snapshot is not mistaken for task-time behavior.
Enable DualGPURunner only when a compute-bound receipt declares at least 2 models loaded in parallel; the supplied data does not establish such a workload.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Make parser diagnostics and positive controls reusable preflight artifacts.
Add task-scoped GPU telemetry and model-count declarations to compute-bound receipts.
meta_reflection: The only compute-bound experiment, Local-SOTA solve-versus-verify remeasurement gated on parser controls, was recorded at 0 minutes; the timing block gives no duration cause, and the locked task-conditioned GPU-idle flag is false despite the idle monitor snapshot. The timing data does not identify any compute-bound task with at least 2 models loaded in parallel; therefore no DualGPURunner miss is established. The 79% estimate is the rounded 66/84 share of the dominant transition and is an upper-bound opportunity, not a measured post-change saving.
